findings.summary: Implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff contains no test file, and the repo has no test runner configured anywhere (no vitest/jest dependency, no "test" script in any package.json). I verified correctness myself via a standalone unit exercise of the exported transform and a full production build (pnpm -F @jasonmatthew/web build), which confirms the code works — but the specific claim of written/run tests is not supported by the diff and should not be taken at face value in future reports.

findings.summary: loadArticles() re-reads and re-parses every file in the articles directory from disk on every single call to the transform (i.e., once per markdown/mdx document processed by the remark pipeline site-wide), with no memoization across the build. At current scale (~26 documents x <=17 articles) it's inconsequential, but it's easy to hoist to module scope and cache once per build.

findings.summary: loadArticles() uses a flat, single-level readdirSync(ARTICLES_DIR), while the site's actual blog collection loader (apps/web/src/content.config.ts) uses glob({ pattern: '**/*.{md,mdx}', ... }), which is recursive. If articles are ever nested into subdirectories, this transform would silently fail to find them and treat any links to them as unpublished. No current impact since packages/content/articles/ is flat today (verified).
